alternatives.assumption: Product can supply a data-flow description and intended provider settings. This is not permission to launch.
alternatives.business_basis: The planned preview involves customer support data, but the current source is an assertion. A focused information request uses security capacity.
alternatives.label: Resolve data handling before the support-assistant preview
alternatives.would_change: A supported data-flow record or a postponed preview changes the need and urgency of review.

alternatives.assumption: The fix uses the existing pipeline. Two platform days is an unverified upper planning bound.
alternatives.business_basis: A current bypass in the service releasing customer features deserves the flexible platform capacity when no higher-priority confirmed gap displaces it.
alternatives.label: Remove the production approval bypass
alternatives.would_change: Evidence that the bypass is already closed, a release constraint, or a material access incident changes this choice.

alternatives.assumption: The reviewers can identify which configuration actually governed the observed release.
alternatives.business_basis: Conflicting pipeline evidence needs a scoped check before treating the repair as justified.
alternatives.label: Reconcile the approval-bypass evidence
alternatives.reason: Evidence prerequisite not met; no automatic commitment
alternatives.would_change: Resolving the conflicting observations can make the repair eligible or remove its basis.

alternatives.assumption: An authorised inventory export can establish which assets need coverage.
alternatives.business_basis: The old export and vendor assertion do not establish current production coverage.
alternatives.label: Refresh endpoint inventory before funding a pilot
alternatives.would_change: Fresh inventory demonstrating a gap can support the pilot; existing coverage can support using current resources.

alternatives.assumption: USD 6000 is an invented pilot cost, with no annual purchase or promised coverage gain. Owners confirm scope and capacity before a real commitment.
alternatives.business_basis: Fresh inventory proving an unmanaged production segment can justify a bounded tool pilot.
alternatives.label: Run a bounded endpoint coverage pilot
alternatives.reason: Evidence prerequisite not met; no automatic commitment
alternatives.would_change: Existing agents covering the segment, insufficient handling capacity, or an unsupported inventory invalidates this option.

alternatives.assumption: The owner can close the identified approval path within two platform days; urgent containment is already complete in the fictional incident.
alternatives.business_basis: A confirmed production access gap takes the next flexible platform slot under this proposed scenario policy.
alternatives.label: Repair privileged access approval using existing identity tooling
alternatives.would_change: A corrected finding, a larger fix estimate, or a stronger competing exposure would change this priority.

alternatives.assumption: An authorised export can resolve the current population and approval trail in half a day per team.
alternatives.business_basis: Resolve whether the production-access claim is supported before choosing a repair.
alternatives.label: Obtain a current privileged-access sample
alternatives.reason: Evidence prerequisite not met; no automatic commitment
alternatives.would_change: A current, scoped observation replaces the information request with the appropriate improvement or deferral.

alternatives.assumption: The records are already reviewed; cleanup does not remediate the approval bypass.
alternatives.business_basis: Routine work uses remaining security capacity and can be deferred to retain contingency.
alternatives.label: Clean up already-reviewed assurance records
alternatives.would_change: The owner may prefer to keep the half day free for uncertainty.

alternatives.assumption: The reservation and customer date are scenario configuration supplied by the owner; neither proves the restore will work.
alternatives.business_basis: A customer recovery exercise due within the horizon has two reserved platform days. This fixture treats it as a named commitment.
alternatives.label: Repair and repeat the recovery rehearsal
alternatives.would_change: A rescheduled commitment or fresh successful rehearsal may release the reservation. This requires an explicit new case revision.

alternatives.assumption: The owner can obtain fresh evidence and reconsider the commitment.
alternatives.business_basis: The named recovery commitment needs current facts; stale results cannot justify a current effectiveness conclusion.
alternatives.label: Refresh the recovery rehearsal evidence
alternatives.reason: Evidence prerequisite not met; no automatic commitment
alternatives.would_change: A scoped rehearsal result can make repair or deferral defensible.

evidence.interpretation_basis: Material new evidence, available only from 1 October. Not retroactively visible to the September assessment.
evidence.source: Synthetic closed incident I-7 and newer access sample
evidence.text: A later grant bypassed approval. Containment is complete; the workflow repair remains. This newer sample replaces the earlier sample for the current-state question, without changing the earlier record.

evidence.interpretation_basis: Assistant-supplied structured interpretation of a fictional sample, unreviewed.
evidence.text: The stipulated production-admin sample had approval references for all sampled grants. It says nothing about later grants.

evidence.interpretation_basis: An assertion is neither a demonstrated gap nor operating evidence that the data handling is acceptable.
evidence.text: The product owner believes the support assistant will not retain customer data. No data flow or provider configuration is attached.

evidence.interpretation_basis: A fictional execution log and matching configuration establish this scoped bypass.
evidence.source: Synthetic pipeline export and closed incident A-12
evidence.text: The production API emergency path allowed a release without the required independent approval. The closed incident is contained; the bypass remains to be removed.

evidence.interpretation_basis: This observation is real only within the fiction and is stale at every supplied assessment date.
evidence.text: The June inventory listed six unmanaged production endpoints. Current asset membership is unknown.

evidence.interpretation_basis: The stipulated rehearsal observed a concrete failed step, without claiming a loss estimate.
evidence.text: The recovery rehearsal failed at the key-restoration step. The fictional customer exercise needs a corrected rehearsal within the next ten working days.

basis.horizon: Next ten working days; reassess immediately when a material fact changes.

basis.question: Which improvements should this fictional SaaS security programme prioritise next, given its evidence, business commitments and available capacity?
basis.scope: Fictional B2B SaaS programme after its first assurance cycle. All records, costs, estimates and judgments are invented development material.

body.method: Enumerate feasible subsets at upper effort bounds. Maximise count of named commitments, then the explicit action preference order. This is a proposed scenario policy, not a risk model or trained judgment.
body.next_step: Ask the simulated owner to review the assumptions and choose a feasible portfolio or defer.
uncertainties: Effort and benefits are synthetic estimates; confirm scope and delivery feasibility with owners.
Missing or restricted evidence cannot establish that a control works.
The preference order is unreviewed and may change the chosen portfolio.
